The first release of **Teletextarr**: teletext-style pages served as live TV channels for Plex and Jellyfin.

Each page is a channel and the page number is the channel number, so you turn pages with your remote's channel buttons or by typing a number, just like Ceefax and Teletext. Because Plex and Jellyfin see it as an ordinary TV tuner, it works in every app they have, including TV apps, consoles and phones.

![Index page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgulliver/teletextarr/v0.1.0/docs/index.png)

## Highlights

### Pages you build yourself
Everything is defined in one YAML file. Each page has a number (100–899), a title, a colour scheme and a type:

| Type | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `index` | Every page with its number, plus the latest headlines from a page you choose |
| `rss` | Stories from one or more RSS or Atom feeds, merged and newest first |
| `weather` | Current conditions and a 1–7 day forecast for one or more places, from Open-Meteo (no API key needed) |
| `xmltv` | Now and next from any XMLTV guide, such as Tunarr or ErsatzTV |
| `media_server` | What's playing and what was just added on Jellyfin and/or Plex, plus free disk space |
| `text` | Your own static text |

### Carousel subpages
Busy pages cycle through subpages as the real carousel did: a headline list first, then one story per subpage. Each page's subpage is set by the clock, so everyone watching sees the same one.

### Weather maps
A weather page can open with a map of any country drawn in mosaic blocks, with live temperatures on the map and a key alongside. You choose the country by ISO code or name. The country outlines are bundled from Natural Earth, so the map needs no internet lookup.

![Weather map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lgulliver/teletextarr/v0.1.0/docs/weather.png)

### Looks the part
- The 40×25 character grid and the eight teletext colours
- Double-height page titles and a header line with a ticking clock
- A coloured Fastext row along the bottom
- The [Bedstead](https://bjh21.me.uk/bedstead/) font, a faithful recreation of the SAA5050 teletext character set

### Works with Plex and Jellyfin
- **Plex:** Teletextarr pretends to be an HDHomeRun tuner, so you add it with Plex's normal DVR setup.
- **Jellyfin:** add it as an M3U tuner.
- **Guide:** an XMLTV guide lists every page as a programme.
- **Previews:** `/preview/<page>.png` shows any page without a TV.

### Light on power
- Nothing is encoded until someone tunes in, and each stream stops as soon as they leave.
- The encoder converts colours once per frame rather than for every duplicated frame, and uses x264's fastest preset. Together these cut CPU per viewer by about two thirds compared with the obvious pipeline.
- A stream is around 350 kbps.
- `server.fps` can lower the frame rate further if your clients accept it.

### Configuration and safety
- **Secrets:** values like `${JELLYFIN_API_KEY}` are read from the environment, so tokens never live in the config file.
- **Validation:** the config is checked on startup with clear errors, and `--check` validates it without starting the server.
- **Customisation:** you can set the brand, the channel name format, each page's banner and channel name, the subpage timings and the Fastext buttons.
- **Privacy:** the server page shows titles only, never who is watching, and `show_now_playing: false` hides that section completely.

## Install

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/lgulliver/teletextarr:0.1.0
```

Images are built for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`. See the [README](https://github.com/lgulliver/teletextarr#quick-start) for a quick start, the full configuration reference and how to add Teletextarr to Plex and Jellyfin.

## Requirements
- Docker, or Python 3.15+ with ffmpeg on the path.
- Plex Media Server with Live TV & DVR (needs Plex Pass), or Jellyfin.

Teletextarr isn't affiliated with the BBC or any broadcaster. It's a tribute to Ceefax and the teletext services that came before it.
